words.meaning: unwilling to change your position or agree to a compromise
words.example: The landlord remained intransigent even after every tenant proposed the same reasonable solution.

words.meaning: ordinary and lacking excitement or imagination
words.example: The assignment sounded prosaic, but it gave her a chance to improve an important process.

words.meaning: requiring great care, effort, or attention to detail
words.example: The editor has exacting standards, so check every citation before submitting the article.

words.meaning: naturally quiet and inclined to say very little
words.example: Our taciturn neighbor rarely chats, but he is always quick to help when someone needs a hand.

phrases.meaning: to adapt calmly when unexpected problems occur
phrases.example: The venue changed at the last minute, but the team rolled with the punches and set up across town.

phrases.meaning: to argue the opposite side in order to test an idea
phrases.example: Let me play devil's advocate: what happens if demand doubles in the first month?

phrases.meaning: to hurt someone deeply with a sharp or personal remark
phrases.example: Her joke about his career cut him to the quick, even though she did not mean to be cruel.

phrases.meaning: to change direction or plans very quickly
phrases.example: Small teams can turn on a dime when customer needs suddenly change.

phrases.term: take the bull by the horns
phrases.meaning: to face a difficult situation directly and decisively
phrases.example: After weeks of confusion, Maya took the bull by the horns and scheduled a meeting with everyone involved.
